_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor from the project's own documentation; no upstream egg.
name: AdGuard Home
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: AdGuard Home is a DNS server that blocks ads and trackers for every device that uses it, managed from a web page on the server's address. Most devices only use DNS on port 53, so give the server a second allocation on port 53 if the node allows it, and set DNS port to it.
startup:
if grep -q '^users: \[\]' AdGuardHome.yaml; then pw="${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"; if [ -z "$pw" ]; then pw=$(tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 </dev/urandom | head -c 20); echo "AdGuard Home's admin is {{ADMIN_USERNAME}}, with the password $pw. Log in and change it."; fi; PW="$pw" U="{{ADMIN_USERNAME}}" perl -i -pe 'BEGIN { @c = ("a".."z", "A".."Z", 0..9, ".", "/"); $h = crypt($ENV{PW}, q($2b$10$) . join("", map { $c[rand 64] } 1..22)); $h =~ /^\$2b\$/ or die "bcrypt failed
" } s/^users: \[\]$/users:
  - name: $ENV{U}
    password: $h/' AdGuardHome.yaml || exit 1; fi; exec ./adguardhome --no-check-update -c AdGuardHome.yaml -w /home/container

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# AdGuard Home: downloads AdGuard Home from its GitHub releases, checked
# against GitHub's SHA-256, and writes a starting AdGuardHome.yaml if there's
# none (the admin account is added when the server first starts). An
# existing configuration and the data folder are never touched.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) echo "AdGuard Home has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))."; exit 1 ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$version" = latest ] || version="v${version#v}"
# gh-release says why when the release doesn't exist or GitHub can't be reached.
tag=$(gh-release tag AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome "$version") || exit 1

if [ -x adguardhome ] && [ "$(cat .adguardhome-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "AdGuard Home $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading AdGuard Home $tag."
    gh-release download AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome "$tag" "AdGuardHome_linux_${arch}.tar.gz" "$work/agh.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/agh.tar.gz" -C "$work"
    install -m 0755 "$work/AdGuardHome/AdGuardHome" adguardhome.new
    mv -f adguardhome.new adguardhome
    echo "$tag" > .adguardhome-version
fi

if [ ! -f AdGuardHome.yaml ]; then
    # The ports are set at every start from the server's allocation and DNS
    # port. users stays empty until the first start adds the admin.
    cat > AdGuardHome.yaml <<'YAML'
http:
  address: 0.0.0.0:3000
users: []
dns:
  bind_hosts:
    - 0.0.0.0
  port: 53
  upstream_dns:
    - https://dns10.quad9.net/dns-query
  bootstrap_dns:
    - 9.9.9.10
    - 149.112.112.10
    - 2620:fe::10
    - 2620:fe::fe:10
# The configuration format of AdGuard Home v0.107.80; newer releases update it.
schema_version: 34
YAML
    echo "Wrote a starting AdGuardHome.yaml."
fi
mkdir -p data
echo "Installed AdGuard Home $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The AdGuard Home release to install, such as 0.107.80, or latest.

variables.name: DNS port
variables.description: The port AdGuard Home answers DNS on: one of the server's allocations, 53 for most devices to use it.

variables.name: Admin username
variables.description: The web page's first user, created when the server first starts.

variables.name: Admin password
variables.description: The first user's password. Leave it empty for a random one, shown in the console at the first start.
